reason: E1 directly supports the formation of Hf- and Zr-enriched short-range clusters upon annealing, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that this ordering reduces electron scattering, sharpens the superconducting transition, or enhances Tc. E2 explicitly states that Tc variations are independent of disorder in the studied HEA, which contradicts the premise that reduced disorder enhances Tc.
premises: Thermal annealing promotes short-range chemical ordering and nanostructural clustering in the HEA
Annealing reduces local inhomogeneities and electron scattering
Reduced disorder leads to a more uniform superconducting phase with a sharper transition
Reduced disorder may slightly enhance the superconducting transition temperature (Tc)
